home.meta_desc: Turn nine standard cell measurements into an objective malignancy estimate with transparent reasoning, batch processing and report export.
hero.title: Clearer, faster insight from cytology measurements
hero.sub: {brand} turns nine standard cell measurements into an objective malignancy estimate, with transparent reasoning, batch processing and report export.
cap.title: Everything you need to analyze with confidence
cap.sub: A focused toolset for fast, reviewable cytology decisions.
cap1.d: Enter nine scores and receive a malignancy probability with a clear benign or malignant verdict.
cap2.d: See which measurements pushed the result up or down, so every estimate can be reviewed.
cap3.d: Upload a CSV file, analyze up to 1,000 samples at once and export the results.
cap4.d: Generate a clean, printable report for each analysis, ready to attach to a case file.
cap5.d: A complete bilingual interface with right-to-left layout and light and dark themes.
cap6.d: Integrate predictions into your own systems with a documented JSON API.
how.title: From measurements to a reviewable result
how1.d: Score the nine cell features from 1 to 10, or import them from a CSV file.
how2.d: A neural network trained on curated cytology data estimates the probability of malignancy.
how3.d: Inspect the verdict and its contributing factors, then export a report.
pt.title: Selected from five competing models
pt.text: Five algorithms were trained and tuned with cross-validation. The neural network identified the most malignant cases and achieved the highest F1-score on held-out data, so it powers the analyzer.
sec.title: Built for privacy and reliability
sec.sub: Sensible defaults that keep your data and your service safe.
sec1.d: Analyzer inputs are processed in memory and are never written to disk.
sec2.d: Fonts, scripts and charts are served from the site itself. No trackers and no external calls.
sec3.d: Strict content security policy, input validation and request rate limiting.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq1.a: Nine cytological scores from 1 to 10: clump thickness, uniformity of cell size and shape, marginal adhesion, single epithelial cell size, bare nuclei, bland chromatin, normal nucleoli and mitoses.
faq2.q: Can I analyze many samples at once?
faq2.a: Yes. Upload a CSV file in the batch tab to analyze up to 1,000 rows at once, then export the results.
faq3.a: No. Measurements are processed in memory to compute the estimate and are not retained.
faq4.a: On held-out test data the model reaches {acc} accuracy, {rec} recall and a {auc} ROC-AUC. The performance page documents the full evaluation.
faq5.q: Can I connect it to my own system?
faq5.a: Yes. A documented JSON API supports single and batch predictions.

cta.sub: Open the analyzer and get a result in seconds.

pf.meta_desc: How the deployed neural network was selected and how it performs on held-out data compared with four other algorithms.
pf.title: Model performance
pf.sub: How the deployed model was selected and how it performs on held-out data.
pf.kpi_s: Results on the held-out test set (139 samples, 48 malignant).
pf.k_accuracy: Share of all samples classified correctly
pf.k_precision: Share of malignant calls that are correct
pf.compare_s: Five algorithms, each tuned with 5-fold cross-validation and scored on the same held-out test set.
pf.cm_s: Confusion matrix on the test set. Select a model to compare.
pf.cv_s: Mean recall and F1 across 3 × 5-fold repeated cross-validation on all 691 samples.
pf.imp_s: Permutation importance on the test set: the drop in F1 when a measurement is shuffled.
pf.p1.d: 691 samples after removing exact duplicates: 453 benign and 238 malignant.
pf.p2.d: Stratified 80:20 split: 552 training and 139 test samples.
pf.p3.d: 5-fold stratified cross-validation on the training set, optimizing F1.
pf.p4.d: Malignant. Recall measures how many malignant cases are identified.
pf.p5.d: Median imputation and standardization fitted on training data only.
pf.sel_d: The ANN, SVM and Random Forest perform within a single test sample of one another. The neural network was selected because it identified the most malignant cases (recall {rec}) while also achieving the highest F1-score and accuracy.
tc.meta_desc: The data, preprocessing, model and validation behind the analyzer, and how each estimate is explained.
tc.title: Technology
tc.sub: How {brand} turns measurements into a reviewable estimate.
tc.data_d: Trained on the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Original) dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository: 699 fine-needle-aspirate samples described by nine cytological scores, reduced to 691 after removing exact duplicates.
tc.prep_d: Missing values are imputed with the training median, identifiers are dropped and features are standardized. Every transformation is fitted on training data only, which prevents leakage into evaluation.
tc.model_d: A multilayer perceptron with one hidden layer of 32 ReLU units, L2 regularization (alpha 0.0001) and the Adam optimizer. Hyperparameters were chosen by grid search with 5-fold cross-validation.
tc.val_d: Stratified hold-out testing and repeated cross-validation confirm stable performance across data splits. Five algorithms were compared on identical data.
tc.expl_d: Every estimate includes the influence of each measurement, computed by replacing it with a typical value and observing the change in the model's log-odds.
tc.use1: Designed for qualified professionals as decision support alongside clinical judgment.
tc.use2: Operates on the nine expert-scored cytological features. It does not analyze images.
tc.use3: Trained on a single curated dataset; performance on other populations should be verified before relying on it.

dv.auth_d: The public endpoints require no key. Requests are rate limited per IP address.
dv.ep1_d: Returns the verdict, probabilities, a confidence band and the influence of every measurement.
dv.ep2_d: Accepts up to {max} rows. Invalid rows are reported individually without failing the whole request.

dv.e503: The analysis model is not available.

pv.meta_desc: What information the website and the analyzer process, and how it is protected.
pv.title: Privacy policy
pv.sub: What information {brand} processes and how it is protected.
pv.1.d: This policy explains what information {brand} processes when you use the website and the analyzer.
pv.2.d: Measurements you enter or upload are sent to the server only to compute estimates. They are processed in memory, are not stored and are not used to train models.
pv.3.d: If you use the contact form, we store your name, email, organization, topic and message in order to reply to you.
pv.4.d: We use one cookie to remember your language and your browser's local storage to remember your theme. We do not use advertising or analytics cookies.
pv.5.d: The site does not load third-party scripts, fonts or trackers and does not share your data with third parties.
pv.6.d: The site applies strict security headers, input validation and rate limiting, and should be served over HTTPS.
pv.7.d: You can clear your browser storage at any time. To request deletion of a contact message, write to us.
pv.8.d: Questions about this policy? Use the contact page.
